Baleba has already agreed personal terms with Manchester United.
Baleba's price dropped from a previous £100m valuation due to uneven performances and an ankle injury.
Tijjani Reijnders left Manchester City for Saudi club Al Qadsiah in a deal worth about €60m.

title: Man Utd's pursuit of Brighton's Carlos Baleba as a 'third midfielder'
author: Simon Stone
content:
![Carlos Baleba playing for Brighton and being challenged for the ball by Arsenal's Declan Rice](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/b1ab/live/efa17790-9bd2-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Carlos Baleba has made 112 appearances for Brighton since joining the club from Lille for Â£23.2m in August 2023
- Published
Manchester United's midfield reconstruction is nearing completion.
After signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa in the space of 24 hours of each other last month, there has been an element of 'will-they, won't-they' about the past five weeks.
At times, it felt the 'third midfielder' search has taken on a life of its own.
Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni was heavily touted, so too Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Roma's Manu Kone. In more recent days, the name of Fulham's Sander Berge has become more prominent. That of Bournemouth's Tyler Adams has never gone away.
United privately played down potential interest in Brighton's Carlos Baleba.
But in a sense, they didn't need to be actively interested in him. Most of the work was done 12 months ago.
Now the first offer has gone in; Â£60m, plus an additional Â£5m. It won't be enough.
Talks are continuing though and the expectation is the transfer will get done.
![Manchester United's new signings Andrey Santos (right) and Youri Tielemans (second right)](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/907/cpsprodpb/64dc/live/7a67f0c0-9bc9-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
New signings Andrey Santos (right) and Youri Tielemans (second right) started alongside each other in midfield for Manchester United against AC Milan in Wroclaw
It is impossible to assess the merits of the actual transfers until the individuals concerned have played often enough to evaluate how well they have done.
However, it is fair to accept United's data and recruitment department have succeeded in reshaping Michael Carrick's midfield.
It was known in January veteran Brazilian Casemiro would leave when his contract expired on 30 June. Ruben Amorim's exit had already seen skipper Bruno Fernandes move into a more advanced role.
With Manuel Ugarte not rated highly despite his Â£50.8m price tag, it meant United went into the summer with Kobbie Mainoo as the only experienced midfielder likely to play a prominent part in the 2026-27 season.
Mainoo's strength is taking the ball in tight spaces and progressing it up the pitch. Santos has screened the defence excellently in pre-season. Tielemans has composure, an excellent passing range, and is determined to increase his goals output.
What the defeat by AC Milan in Wroclaw at the weekend highlighted was a lack of energy; a player in the old box-to-box mould. Baleba's main strength is his ability to cover the ground quickly.
If the deal goes through, and when Baleba has recovered from an ankle injury sustained in pre-season that is expected to keep him out for another couple of weeks, Carrick will have variety and options, which also include Mason Mount, Scotland World Cup squad member Tyler Fletcher and, in extremis, Fernandes.
![Manchester United spent the summer of 2022 trying to sign Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong but eventually signed Casemiro instead](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/900/cpsprodpb/d973/live/f6f725c0-9bc9-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Manchester United spent the summer of 2022 trying to sign Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong but eventually gave up
The Baleba situation also highlights a strategic change.
In the past, United have almost trailed the players they want to sign, then spent ages trying to complete a deal â or not.
Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong was a case in point in 2022. Erik ten Hag felt certain he could do the deal even though United's recruitment staff were being told it was impossible.
It was well into August before the club admitted defeat; with defeats by Brighton and Brentford triggering the Â£70m deal for Casemiro.
This summer, there has been stealth behind their work. It suited them for talk around England's Elliot Anderson to obscure what they were thinking around initial midfield targets as they knew the Nottingham Forest man would be financially beyond their reach.
The Santos deal was wrapped up within a week. The Tielemans one was less than that.
There has been consideration given to Mount being the 'third midfielder' because of his exceptional form in the early part of pre-season.
However, although his early exit in the encounter with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg on 8 August was described as 'precautionary', Mount has still to return from the foot injury, which would only have heightened concerns around his injury record.
Baleba was supposedly off the radar as a third midfielder. Tchouameni, Scott, Kone, Berge and Adams were the ones being monitored. Now United have made their move, it would be a surprise if the transfer was not concluded swiftly.
Evidently, Old Trafford's recruitment plans are now being controlled to a far tighter degree than was previously the case.
Premier League proven - but a left-back still needed
Of the four players they signed in 2025, striker Benjamin Sesko and goalkeeper Senne Lammens were the only two who were not bought from Premier League clubs.
The ease with which Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha settled into their new surroundings must have played a part in shaping thinking at Old Trafford this summer.
Cunha and Tielemans had release clauses. Mbeumo and Santos did not, neither does Baleba.
There is an argument buying from Premier League clubs costs more because they are all relatively rich. The premium, in theory, limits the risk of players failing to settle. It seems Manchester United feel the extra is worth paying.
"We want more, we need more," Carrick stressed last week.
Baleba cannot be the end. It is accepted the need for a new left-back is acute.
No-one knows who it will be at this stage. But it is fair to assume there will be one.
summary: Manchester United are nearing the completion of their midfield reconstruction after making an initial bid of £60m plus £5m for Brighton's Carlos Baleba to fill their 'third midfielder' role. The club has already added Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans this summer, altering their recruitment approach to be more stealthy and focused on Premier League-proven talent. Despite these additions, manager Michael Carrick acknowledges that further reinforcements, specifically a new left-back, are still required.
key_points: Manchester United have made a £60m plus £5m opening offer for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba, with expectations that the transfer will be completed.
United previously strengthened their midfield during the summer by signing Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.
The club's recent recruitment strategy has shifted toward stealth and acquiring players with Premier League experience to reduce settling-in risks.
Baleba is currently recovering from an ankle injury sustained in pre-season that is expected to keep him out for another couple of weeks.
Club officials and manager Michael Carrick accept that an acute need remains for Manchester United to sign a new left-back.

title: Manchester United and Brighton closing in on deal for Carlos Baleba
author: David Ornstein
content:
Manchester United and Brighton & Hove Albion are closing in on a deal for midfielder Carlos Baleba.
United have made an offer of around £60million (€70m, $81m) plus £5m in add-ons which is felt to be below what Brighton would be seeking to sell.
Amicable talks continue with all parties working towards finding an agreement for the Cameroon international to move to Old Trafford.
Advertisement
The 22-year-old is currently working his way back to fitness after an ankle ligament injury but the issue is not considered serious or expected to keep him out long-term.
Midfield has been an area of significant focus for United in the transfer market this summer.
Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have already arrived from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively while a deal for Atalanta midfielder Ederson was also agreed before the club backed out over injury concerns surrounding the Brazil international’s knee.
They were also keen on Elliot Anderson before the England international opted to move to rivals Manchester City instead.
Should a move for Baleba progress he would join Tielemans, Santos, Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes as first-team options for head coach Michael Carrick.
Manuel Ugarte is currently sidelined with the knee injury he suffered during the World Cup with Uruguay while Mason Mount has also missed the final two games of pre-season.
Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in the summer of 2023 and has played 112 times for the south-coast club. Last season he made 35 appearances in total for the club, missing several due to his participation at the Africa Cup of Nations.
![How Carlos Baleba would fit at Manchester United and what else to know](https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2026/08/19091900/GettyImages-2261791761-e1787145568908-1024x681.jpg?width=400&quality=70) 
Why United have wanted Baleba
Analysis by Manchester United correspondent Laurie Whitwell
After United made significant work to explore a transfer for Baleba last summer, the midfielder had a difficult campaign with Brighton. But The Athletic reported in April how signing him was still highly plausible due to his impressive displays in his first two seasons in the Premier League and his underlying data.
United also watched him play for Cameroon during the Africa Cup of Nations, alongside Bryan Mbeumo, where Baleba was viewed as having a positive tournament across five matches. United rate his metrics as a good fit for the squad in terms of ground coverage, possession-winning and passing.
Given his left-footedness, Baleba could also potentially provide cover at left-back.
![](https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2026/08/19045943/Carlos-Baleba_player_roles_2025-26.png)
Last season Baleba was substituted off in 15 Premier League games, including at half-time on four occasions. It seems undeniable that United’s pursuit last summer turned his head, and his form at Brighton was partially affected. He also worked through some injury niggles. When appearing for Cameroon, he regained his confidence. Brighton staff supported him throughout.
Advertisement
Baleba completed 90 minutes only three times, but one of those was in the 3-0 win over Chelsea, when he played well, winning the ball in the penalty box from Robert Sanchez to set up Jack Hinshelwood for a big chance. He started the next three matches and came off the bench against United on the final day.
Last summer, when Baleba’s stock was high after two excellent seasons, United would have gone to £75m but Brighton wanted more than £100m. Now, United are set to strike a deal for significantly below that.
summary: Manchester United and Brighton & Hove Albion are in amicable talks regarding a transfer for midfielder Carlos Baleba. United have submitted an offer of £60 million plus £5 million in add-ons, which is currently below Brighton's valuation. The 22-year-old Cameroon international is recovering from an ankle ligament injury that is not considered long-term.
key_points: Manchester United made an offer of around £60 million plus £5 million in add-ons for Carlos Baleba.
Baleba is currently recovering from an ankle ligament injury that is not expected to keep him out long-term.
United's pursuit of midfield reinforcements has included summer arrivals Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.
Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in 2023 and has made 112 appearances for the club.

title: Nick Kyrgios suspended from tennis after testing positive for cocaine
author: Matt Hughes
content:
The former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios has been suspended after testing positive for cocaine. The 31-year-old Australian revealed on Instagram on Wednesday that he had “made a huge mistake”. His suspension was confirmed by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) shortly afterwards.
Kyrgios tested positive while playing at an ATP 250 event in Mallorca in June, with the presence of cocaine in his system confirmed by tests at a World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada) laboratory last month. Under ITIA regulations, provisional suspensions are mandatory for positive tests for cocaine, although Kyrgios has the right of appeal.
“I wanted you to hear this from me first,” Kyrgios wrote. “I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine. I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it. I’m sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I’m sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I’m deeply disappointed in myself.
“I’m not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I’ve been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn’t been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.
“I’ve always said I didn’t choose tennis – tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I’ve ever had to face. At times I’ve felt helpless and alone. None of that excuses what I did.
“However, the good news is that this has given me a wake up call. For the next 28 days, I’ll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.
![Nick Kyrgios smashes against Novak Djokovic in the Wimbledon men’s singles final in 2022](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/d355a30fbefb8c6d722b64956f270df232ff5948/0_0_5515_3567/master/5515.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
“I’d ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family. I’m sorry. I’ll do the work and come back better.”
The ITIA confirmed an unspecified provisional suspension for Kyrgios, with its length to be determined by whether the substance was taken in or out of competition.
In 2017, Britain’s Dan Evans was given a 12-month ban after testing positive for cocaine during the Barcelona Open, but Wada rules have since changed and stipulate a three-month suspension for out of competition offences. This ban can be reduced to one month if the athlete agrees to undertake an approved programme of rehabilitation, the route taken by the South Africa fast bowler Kasigo Rabada after he tested positive for cocaine last year.
after newsletter promotion
“Kyrgios provided a sample during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca, Spain, on 22 June 2026,” the ITIA statement said. “On 17 July 2026, a World Anti-Doping Agency -accredited laboratory confirmed the presence of benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.
“Cocaine is a stimulant and substance of abuse on the Wada Prohibited List and is banned in competition under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme. Because of the nature of the substance, a provisional suspension is mandatory and has been in place since 4 August 2026.”
Kyrgios has been a controversial figure throughout his career, which peaked with a 2022 Wimbledon final defeat to Novak Djokovic having previously achieved a highest world ranking of 13 in 2016.
In recent years injuries have restricted Kyrgios’s appearances and he has not played in a grand slam since the 2025 Australian Open, although he did take part in the “Battle of the Sexes” against Aryna Sabalenka in Dubai last December.
summary: Former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios has received a provisional suspension from tennis after testing positive for cocaine during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca in June. The Australian player announced the failed test on Instagram, taking full responsibility and citing physical and mental struggles resulting from recent injuries. The International Tennis Integrity Agency confirmed the mandatory provisional suspension, which has been in place since August 4, 2026.
key_points: Nick Kyrgios tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a cocaine metabolite, in June 2026 at an event in Mallorca.
The International Tennis Integrity Agency confirmed a mandatory provisional suspension beginning on August 4, 2026.
Kyrgios publicly admitted to the mistake on Instagram, apologizing to fans and acknowledging the toll of recent injuries.
Cocaine is a banned substance of abuse under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme and Wada Prohibited List.

title: Nick Kyrgios provisionally suspended from tennis after testing positive for cocaine
author: Amy Lofthouse
content:
![Nick Kyrgios watches on during January's Australian Open](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/9430/live/d82d7ee0-9ba7-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios has won one and lost three of his four singles matches this year
- Published
Nick Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended from tennis after testing positive for cocaine.
The Australian submitted a sample during the Mallorca Open on 22 June that was later found to contain benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.
Former world number 13 Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended, external since 4 August.
The International Tennis Integrity Agency said Kyrgios could appeal against the provisional suspension "but has not done so to date".
In a post on Instagram, Kyrgios said he made "a huge mistake" and takes "full responsibility" for it.
Under the suspension, Kyrgios cannot play, coach at or attend Grand Slams or any events sanctioned by the men's and women's tennis tours pending the outcome of a tribunal.
Kyrgios could be banned for up to four years - but if he can prove he took the drug outside of a competition, the maximum ban he would face is three months.

title: Hadjar in doubt for Dutch GP after wrist injury
author: Josh Suttill
content:
Isack Hadjar is likely to miss Formula 1’s Dutch Grand Prix due to injury, meaning Liam Lawson could make a surprise return to Red Bull Racing this weekend.
First reported by Dutch outlet De Telegraaf, Hadjar has picked up a wrist injury over F1’s summer break, which has put his participation at Zandvoort into major doubt. The Race understands Hadjar being sidelined is the most likely outcome but that a final decision has not yet been made.
No decision has been made on who replaces him but if Hadjar is unable to participate, Racing Bulls driver Lawson could make an unlikely return to Red Bull Racing, where he lasted just two races before being demoted at the start of 2025.
Ironically Lawson's F1 racing career began with a Dutch GP injury call-up three years ago, when then AlphaTauri driver Daniel Ricciardo broke his hand in a practice crash.
The shuffle would also hand Yuki Tsunoda an F1 return, as he’d take Lawson’s place at Racing Bulls, a team he made 89 starts for before his own short-lived promotion to Red Bull Racing last year, in place of Lawson.
Tsunoda is currently serving as the team’s reserve driver, having been so far unable to secure an F1 race seat since losing his Red Bull Racing drive at the end of last year. He has been linked this week to an IndyCar future in place of Indianapolis 500 winner Felix Rosenqvist, as Rosenqvist returns to McLaren’s IndyCar team for 2027.
Zandvoort was the scene of Hadjar’s first F1 podium last year, and he’d been putting together a solid 2026 season, with every indication being that he’d be retained in Red Bull's main team for 2027.
If he misses Zandvoort, Hadjar would have two weeks to recover before the next race at Monza.
summary: Isack Hadjar is in major doubt for the Dutch Grand Prix due to a wrist injury sustained during the summer break, though a final decision has not yet been made. His potential absence could lead to Liam Lawson returning to Red Bull Racing. Consequently, Yuki Tsunoda would step into Lawson's seat at Racing Bulls.
key_points: Isack Hadjar is likely to miss the Dutch Grand Prix due to a wrist injury.
Liam Lawson could make a surprise return to Red Bull Racing if Hadjar cannot race.
Yuki Tsunoda would take Lawson's place at Racing Bulls.
Hadjar would have two weeks to recover before the next race at Monza if he misses Zandvoort.

title: After a long wait: the Premier League breaks its silence over the Manchester City case | Goal.com
author: Khaled Mahmoud
content:
Richard Masters, the chief executive of the Premier League, has admitted the verdict in Manchester City's financial charges case "has taken longer than expected". He also insisted he remains fully committed to keeping the proceedings confidential until a final decision is reached.
The case dates back three years. The Premier League charged the Sky Blues with breaching financial fair play rules across nine seasons, specifically the period from 2009 to 2018, during which the club lifted three Premier League titles. City's hierarchy have flatly denied every charge and rejected any suggestion of wrongdoing.
At the heart of the case is an alleged failure to provide accurate financial information to the league over those nine years, along with a refusal to cooperate with the investigations into the club's finances. Both parties sat through hearings that ran for 12 weeks before an independent three-member commission between September and December of 2024. Nearly two years on, no verdict has landed.
Quizzed on the latest developments during the launch event for the new Premier League season (2026-2027), Masters told the Sky News network: "There is nothing I can add at the present time. Our rules are entirely clear on this matter, and I must keep everything confidential until we are ready to issue the decision and announce it with full clarity."
By way of explanation, the chief executive added: "I cannot provide any updates regarding the timing or the progress of the procedures. The only path available to us is to let the legal process take its natural course. I fully understand the frustration that exists, as the matter has indeed taken longer than expected."
![Manchester City crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/YaWwRy_S6TKMuwJHBvDbR.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg)
![AFC Bournemouth crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/FS7UO4BdZPMJrL5MlqxyL.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg)
Was he angry at the length of the deliberations? Masters said not. "Of course not. I previously stated that the commission needs the time and sufficient space to carry out its work. In the end, the role of the Premier League is limited to bringing the charges, when sufficient evidence is available, before an independent commission to enable it to establish the truth, which is something that should not be constrained by the length of time it takes to reach that truth."
summary: Premier League Chief Executive Richard Masters has acknowledged that the financial charges case against Manchester City has taken longer than expected. Masters reaffirmed his commitment to maintaining confidentiality regarding the proceedings until an independent commission reaches a final decision. Manchester City denies all allegations of breaching financial fair play rules across the nine-season period in question.
key_points: Premier League CEO Richard Masters admitted the Manchester City financial case is taking longer than expected.
Manchester City was charged with breaching financial fair play rules across nine seasons from 2009 to 2018.
The club denies all charges and any suggestion of financial wrongdoing.
Masters confirmed that proceedings will remain strictly confidential until a final decision is issued by the independent commission.

title: Liverpool 'offered Barcola discount' as agreement reached in PSG talks
author: Alex Young
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Jeff Bezos nears deal to buy more than 30% stake in Liverpool.](https://cdn.ex.co/transformations-account/production/761715bb-261d-4032-af09-a493a82bd926/2b831c96-e859-577d-b7b5-90b0e62a93e2/thumbnail-360.webp)
Barcola is a key target for the Reds, and has also been linked with Arsenal, as new manager Andoni Iraola pushes to strengthen his forward line following the departure of Mohamed Salah.
The 23-year-old has reportedly made it clear that he is open to a move to Anfield, with personal terms not expected to be a problem. Liverpool see Barcola as a player capable of making an immediate impact on both flanks.
PSG team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye is also a target, with French publication RMC Sport reporting on Monday that Liverpool have agreed personal terms with the young striker as they continue talks with PSG over a sensational double raid.
![Bradley Barcola](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/6/28/barcola180826a.jpeg?trim=62,0,63,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
The major obstacle, though, has been the transfer fee for Barcola.
PSG had previously placed a valuation of about £145m on the France international, a figure Liverpool were unwilling to meet. However, reports now suggest that the French champions have reduced their demands to as low as £110m, potentially bringing the two clubs closer to an agreement.
French outlet Jeunes Footeux report that PSG’s recent transfer business - signing the likes of Ferran Torres and Mika Godts in bolster the attack - means the demands placed upon Barcola’s head could be relaxed.
The Ligue 1 giants have now invested around €150 million in their summer recruitment, although their spending has been offset by player sales so remain under no immediate pressure to offload further players.
There has been further encouragement for Liverpool from PSG’s recent team selections. Barcola was left on the bench for the UEFA Super Cup win over Aston Villa, and out of the squad entirely for the Trophée des Champions defeat to Lens at the weekend. Mbaye was also absent.
Despite hope over a possible discount for Barcola, Liverpool must still agree a fee with PSG and remain locked in negotiations. There is no suggestion that Liverpool will pay PSG’s asking price.
summary: Liverpool are pursuing a potential double transfer for PSG attackers Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye. While PSG previously valued Barcola at £145m, reports suggest their demands may drop to £110m following recent summer signings. Liverpool have reportedly agreed personal terms with Mbaye and remain in ongoing negotiations with PSG regarding Barcola.
key_points: Liverpool are targeting PSG forward Bradley Barcola and teammate Ibrahim Mbaye.
PSG have reportedly lowered their asking price for Barcola from £145m down to £110m.
Liverpool have already agreed personal terms with young striker Ibrahim Mbaye.
Barcola was recently left out of PSG's starting lineup and matchday squad for key fixtures.
Negotiations between Liverpool and PSG over transfer fees are still ongoing.

title: England vs Pakistan: A huge challenge, but Joe Root can finish captaincy story
author: Stephan Shemilt
content:
![England captain Joe Root trains at Headingley](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/c83b/live/dbff93c0-9b1e-11f1-a8a4-83462463c9fa.jpg)
Returning captain Joe Root has already led in 65 Tests, an England record
- Published
Of all the places for England to begin a new era, Headingley is the most difficult to shake off the memory of Ben Stokes.
In the city of Stokes' greatest miracle, the home side must plot a future without a captain, all-rounder and talisman, starting against Pakistan on Wednesday.
Yet, for all Stokes' legendary achievements it cannot be said his four-year spell as England captain ended with the team in a better state than he found it.
Stokes inherited a team that had won only one in 17 and exited with two wins in 10. New, old skipper Joe Root might wonder about the chaos his old mucker has left behind.
England have sacked Brendon McCullum as Test coach and replaced him with Stephen Fleming, only Fleming is not yet in post, meaning Marcus Trescothick is interim boss, all while McCullum remains floating around as white-ball gaffer.
It leaves this three-match series against Pakistan with a feeling of impermanence, not unlike Root's last tour as captain in the West Indies in 2022. England lost 1-0 with Paul Collingwood as temporary coach and Root resigned as captain soon after.
Root was left broken by his first, five-year, stint in the top job. There was a time when he would not have considered returning as skipper. Still, here he is on his home ground, ready to go again, smiling, excited and energised by his comeback.
Plenty will wonder why he wants to put himself through it all once more. Well, consider what it must be like to give up the England captaincy, to admit you can no longer do a dream job.
Root will have regrets from his first attempt, and maybe a sense of unresolved business. How irresistible it must be to get a second chance that very few are afforded.
If we thought Stokes' destiny was to end with an Ashes win next summer, then the all-rounder was unable to finish his story. Now Root has the opportunity to finish his.
The Yorkshireman has acknowledged one challenge of this captaincy is how some may view his first reign. Root was regularly self-deprecating about his own leadership during Stokes' tenure.
Yes, there was the one win in 17 to end it all, but before that, Root's record was pretty good: 26 wins from his first 47 matches in charge gave a success rate of 55%. As a comparison, Stokes won 54% of his Tests as skipper, Michael Vaughan 51% and Mike Brearley 58%.
How do England move on from Stokes?
Covid destroyed Root's team, and there are other reasons why Root might also feel he didn't get a fair shake first time around. His tenure as captain coincided with a prioritisation of white-ball cricket and, when he stood in for Stokes against New Zealand in June, he admitted to some envy at not getting the chance to work alongside McCullum.
Not that everything went against Root. One could argue that, given the players at his disposal, he should have had a better record as captain.
Peak Stokes, England's two greatest bowlers in James Anderson and Stuart Broad, plus the luxury of further all-rounders Chris Woakes and Moeen Ali. Root did not get to lead the best version of Alastair Cook, but the late-career Sir Chef would improve the current England team.
Root may feel he is better placed to captain England now, yet he is taking over if not a worse, then certainly a much more inexperienced team. Perhaps he will find this group easier to mould in his image. In his first Test as captain, in 2017, Root was the third-youngest player in the XI. In 2026, at the age of 35, he is comfortably the oldest.
For plenty of supporters the main worry will be the possibility of a detrimental effect the captaincy could have on Root's batting, and it is true that his average with the armband - 46.7 - is some way off a lofty 53.3 without.
That discrepancy is mainly because of a poor run in the middle of his first stint as skipper. Root averaged 37 in 2019, the year before things started going wrong for England during Covid.
In 2021, mid-pandemic and with the team falling apart, Root racked up 1,708 runs - the most by any England batter in a calendar year. He later explained that batting, being in the middle, was the only time he got any peace.
Root remains England's best player. Since the beginning of the Bazball era, he has scored almost 1,000 more Test runs than any other batter in the world. In the same period, he has moved second on the all-time list of run-scorers, with Sachin Tendulkar now in his sights.
Catchin' Sachin is the sub-plot to Root's second stint as captain, and he is adamant he can juggle the jobs of leadership and run-scoring.
England v Pakistan
First Test, Headingley
19-23 August, 11:00 BST
Ball-by-ball commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra and BBC Sounds. Live text updates, radio commentary and in-play video clips on the BBC Sport website and app. Today at the Test on BBC Two (BBC Four on 21 Aug) and BBC iPlayer from 19:00 BST.
His job as a leader will be to mould a group of players whose education in Test cricket was hampered by the informal approach of Stokes and McCullum. That point about Stokes not leaving the England squad in a better place than he found it? Root's team have questions about an opener and wicketkeeper, a makeshift number three, no obvious all-round option and are without a world-class spinner.
England start as favourites against a Pakistan team that has not won a series in this country in 30 years and will be without their own captain in Leeds, the injured Babar Azam.
Pakistan have, however, played more Tests in July and August than England â a 1-1 draw against West Indies. In seamer Mohammad Abbas and spinner Sajid Khan, they have bowlers who have caused England trouble in the past. If the tourists can get enough runs, it will be a competitive series.
After this, it gets very difficult for England. The winter includes trips to South Africa and Bangladesh, and a one-off pink-ball shootout against Australia.
Speaking of the Aussies, they will surely be better than they showed in defeat by Bangladesh when they arrive for the Ashes next summer. After that, England go to India in early 2028. It all adds up to a devilishly difficult first 18 months of Root's second tenure.
For all his runs, records, and milestones, perhaps rebuilding this England team in the face of the tasks ahead represents one of the greatest challenges of his storied career.
On top of that, Root has acknowledged the work his team have to do to rebuild their reputation with the public after a string of off-field misdemeanours. "Be good role models and good human beings," he has said to his players.
They should look no further than their captain for an example, for Root is one of the best.
summary: Joe Root has returned for a second stint as England's Test captain, starting with a three-match series against Pakistan at Headingley. He takes over a team left in a chaotic and inexperienced state following the departures of Ben Stokes and coach Brendon McCullum. Despite concerns over his batting average while captaining and the tough fixtures ahead, Root is energized and aims to finish his leadership story while chasing Sachin Tendulkar's run-scoring record.
key_points: Joe Root returns as England men's Test captain for a second stint, having previously led the team in a record 65 Tests.
England faces Pakistan in a three-match series at Headingley under interim coach Marcus Trescothick, following the exits of Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum.
Root takes over a younger, more inexperienced squad facing a challenging schedule that includes upcoming tours to South Africa, Bangladesh, and Australia.
At 35 years old, Root is England's oldest player and aims to balance leadership duties while pursuing Sachin Tendulkar's all-time run-scoring record.

title: Jeff Bezos: Amazon founder's consortium bought close to 40% of Liverpool
author: Aadam Patel
content:
![Jeff Bezos points to head](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1008/cpsprodpb/88c0/live/1f977b10-9b0c-11f1-bb80-c1b1e1adeea5.jpg)
Jeff Bezos is part of the 1892 Holdings consortium
- Published
A consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos bought close to 40% of Liverpool from Fenway Sports Group (FSG).
It was initially reported that 1892 Holdings had bought about a third of the club, but - as first reported by The Athletic, external - it is actually about 38%.
There is also an option for the consortium to buy a controlling stake in Liverpool in the next 12 months, though that does not involve a formal commitment.
In a statement on Friday, FSG confirmed it had entered into a "definitive agreement" for the sale of a "strategic minority investment" to 1892 Holdings.
The group - named after Liverpool's founding year - is led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia and also includes Bezos and billionaire Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.
Bhatia will become Liverpool's vice-chairman and join an expanded board pending regulatory approval.
The son-in-law of Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal, he had been a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers for 18 years before relinquishing his stake in the club last month.
The deal is understood to value Liverpool between Â£5bn and Â£6bn.
summary: A consortium named 1892 Holdings, which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, has acquired close to 40% of Liverpool from Fenway Sports Group. The group is led by Amit Bhatia, who will become Liverpool's vice-chairman pending regulatory approval. The deal values the football club between £5bn and £6bn, and the consortium holds an option to purchase a controlling stake within the next 12 months.
key_points: A consortium including Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin bought approximately 38% of Liverpool.
Fenway Sports Group confirmed the definitive agreement for a strategic minority investment by 1892 Holdings.
Amit Bhatia leads the consortium and will join Liverpool's board as vice-chairman.
The consortium has an option to acquire a controlling stake in the club within the next 12 months.
The transaction values Liverpool between £5bn and £6bn.

title: Transfer news LIVE: Alvarez to Arsenal, Barcola bid, Fernandes talks
author: Alex Young
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) ![Bradley Barcola, Bruno Fernandes, Julian Alvarez]() The summer window is kicking into another gear as the likes of Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham work on deals to improve their squads before the start of the new Premier League season. The Gunners continue to be linked with Julian Alvarez and Victor Osimhen to bolster their attack, while Ezri Konsa and Jarrel Quansah continue to be of interest in defence. Man United are aware of interest in Bruno Guimaraes, amid reports of a £43million bid from Galatasaray, and are said to be interested in Adam Wharton and Kim Min-jae. Meanwhile, Liverpool have agreed personal terms with Ibrahim Mbaye as they take another huge step towards a double deal including Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola. Chelsea are braced for a Man City bid for Enzo Fernandez following Rodri’s move to Barcelona, while Pedro Neto has admirers in Saudi Arabia. Tottenham are closing in on the signing of Savinho and hope to then add Cody Gakpo to their forward line. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below! Latest transfer news and rumours Live updates Newcastle still keen on £50m Lucas Bergvall Newcastle United remain interested in signing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall. According to the Daily Mail, Matthias Jaissle’s side are considering Bergvall as a potential replacement for former captain Bruno Guimaraes. The 20-year-old is regarded as one of Europe’s most promising young midfielders, but earlier this summer asked to leave after not being guaranteed regular first-team football. Tottenham are understood to value Bergvall at around £50m. Liverpool to submit new Bradley Barcola bid Liverpool are set to submit a fresh bid for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola as they close in on a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye. According to RMC Sport, a deal to sign Mbaye is progressing quickly after the player reached an agreement with Liverpool over a five-year contract. Liverpool are also deep in talks over Barcola, with a new bid expected this week. PSG want a potential club-record fee for the France star. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/12/01KZRTW82CCT9NK9YH60MGADZ1.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Atletico send Alvarez transfer message to Arsenal after 'Arteta talks' Julian Alvarez has been left out of Atletico Madrid's first La Liga game of the season, but the striker remains not for sale amid interest from Barcelona and Arsenal. The Argentine has been Barcelona's top transfer target all summer, with the player having repeatedly voiced his desire to move to the Camp Nou. Arsenal have long been interested in the former Manchester City forward, with Mikel Arteta reportedly driving the club's interest, but it is Barca were Alvarez wishes to go. Atletico have other ideas, and have repeated privately and publicly ruled out a summer exit for the striker. “It’s like when you go to court, that’s it, there’s nothing more to it. We’re looking after both the person and the player, and we understand that he is not in the right condition to play in this match." ![Julian Alvarez](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/11/44/alvarez.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Tottenham set Richarlison transfer stance Tottenham will demand a sizeable fee if they are to sell Richarlison before the close of the summer transfer window, writes Sam Tabuteau. There had been concerns that Spurs could lose the Brazilian striker, who is attracting interest from Everton, on the cheap with a year remaining on his current contract. But Standard Sport understands that Spurs retain the option to extend Richarlison’s contract by an extra 12 months, meaning they will not be forced into a cut-price sale. Spurs signed Richarlison from Everton in a deal worth around £60million in 2022. Richarlison finished last season as Spurs’ top goalscorer in all competitions, netting 11 times in the Premier League as the north London club narrowly avoided relegation. Despite playing a pivotal role in Spurs keeping their Premier League status, the 29-year-old continues to be linked with a move away. A return to his homeland, or former club Everton, have been mooted. ![

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/15/14/01M02V3KG7EVNXGMVVCAD3Z7V6.jpg?trim=0,0,226,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Man United, Newcastle and Tottenham monitor Edmond Tapsoba Manchester United, Newcastle United and Tottenham are monitoring Bayer Leverkusen defender Edmond Tapsoba. According to Fussballdaten, Leverkusen would be willing to discuss a deal for the 27-year-old centre-back at around €50m (£42.7m), despite his contract running until 2031. Tapsoba has been an important player for Leverkusen since joining from Vitória Guimarães in 2020 and has made more than 270 competitive appearances for the Bundesliga club. All three Premier League clubs are reportedly in contact with the Burkina Faso international’s representatives as they assess the possibility of a summer move. Chelsea demand £100m for Pedro Neto Chelsea are demanding a fee of £100m for Pedro Neto, Dom Smith reports. The Portuguese winger is attracting interest from Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, having also been linked with the likes of Manchester City, Tottenham and Liverpool this summer. However, Chelsea are not actively looking to sell Neto and would ask for an eye-watering £100m to entertain any prospect of a sale. Chelsea’s high valuation of Neto has been influenced by the inflated winger market elsewhere in Europe. Man Utd being new contract talks with Bruno Fernandes Manchester United have opened contract talks with Bruno Fernandes and insist he is not for sale at any price amid interest from Turkish giants Galatasaray, writes Sam Tabuteau. Standard Sport understands that United are determined to keep hold of their influential captain this summer and have held preliminary talks over a new deal. Fernandes’ current contract at Old Trafford expires next summer, but United, who have the option to extend it by a further 12 months, are relaxed about the situation and already in the process of negotiating fresh terms The Portuguese international enjoyed a stellar campaign last season as United qualified for the Champions League, breaking the single season assist record in the Premier League. Fernandes is viewed as a critical part of manager Michael Carrick’s plans. However, interest has begun to build in his services with clubs aware that he could leave on a free transfer next summer There was previously a £57million release clause in Fernandes’ contract, but that expired this summer and United have now made their stance on the former Sporting midfielder clear. ![

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/17/20/01M087ESDKKD461P1X06HMC9VS.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Official! Newcastle sign Amar Dedic Newcastle have signed defender Amar Dedic from Benfica in a deal worth around £30m. Dedic has signed a five-year deal to reunite with manager Matthias Jaissle, with whom he previously won the Austrian title at Red Bull Salzburg in 2023. "It's a special feeling and a really big honour for me to join Newcastle United," he said after the move was announced on Tuesday, his 24th birthday. "I'm really happy to be here and can't wait to start playing for the club and the amazing fans. "Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me. We know each other well. He knows what I can bring on the pitch and I'm really happy to be playing for him again. "Playing Premier League football at St James' Park is going to be really special. Every game feels like a big occasion, with an amazing atmosphere. I'm really excited to get started." Arsenal monitor Marc Pubill and attacking targets Arsenal remain keen to strengthen their defence and attack during the final days of the window. The Gunners made enquiries about Atletico Madrid defender Marc Pubill before the summer transfer window, but the Spanish club are equally determined to keep the 23-year-old. The Athletic report that left wing is Arsenal’s priority, though could move for a right-sided forward if the right opportunity becomes available. Kenan Yildiz and Julian Alvarez remain long-term targets, with Arsenal waiting to see if either becomes available before deciding whether to pursue alternative options. Manchester United open Bruno Fernandes contract talks Manchester United are in contract talks with Bruno Fernandes after the midfielder received a lucrative proposal from Galatasaray. According to The Athletic, the Turkish club offered the 31-year-old a salary of €20m (£17.1m) per year, but Fernandes wants to remain at United and is discussing a new deal. His current contract runs until 2027, with an option for a further year. A €65m release clause available to foreign clubs has also now expired. United are not open to selling Fernandes and maintain they have received no contact from other clubs over the Portugal international.
summary: Premier League clubs are actively working on summer transfer deals and squad improvements as the window progresses. Key developments include Liverpool nearing a double deal involving Ibrahim Mbaye and Bradley Barcola, Manchester United opening contract talks with Bruno Fernandes, and Newcastle United completing the signing of Amar Dedic from Benfica for £30 million. Meanwhile, clubs like Arsenal, Chelsea, and Tottenham face high valuations or resistance from parent clubs regarding targets such as Julian Alvarez and Pedro Neto.
key_points: Newcastle United signed defender Amar Dedic from Benfica on a five-year deal for approximately £30 million.
Liverpool have agreed personal terms with Ibrahim Mbaye and are preparing a fresh bid for PSG winger Bradley Barcola.
Manchester United have opened contract talks with Bruno Fernandes and insist he is not for sale amid interest from Galatasaray.
Atletico Madrid have ruled out a summer exit for Julian Alvarez despite strong interest from Arsenal and Barcelona.
Chelsea have placed a £100 million valuation on Pedro Neto amid interest from Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal.

title: Guardiola’s row with Walker at Manchester City revealed in new Amazon documentary
author: PA Media; Guardian staff reporter
content:
Pep Guardiola clashed with his captain and almost broke down in tears as he railed at players during his worst run as Manchester City manager.
Guardiola stood down at the end of last season after winning 20 trophies in a 10-year spell at the Etihad Stadium. One of the lowest points of his glittering reign came during a testing run in the autumn of 2024, when City lost nine times and won only once in 13 games. Guardiola outwardly showed signs of strain, notably when he scratched his face after City surrendered a 3-0 lead to draw 3-3 with Feyenoord in the Champions League.
Behind closed doors he was also angry and upset with his players, as shown in a new fly-on-the-wall Amazon Prime documentary, A Beautiful Obsession.
At one point he argued in the dressing room with then captain Kyle Walker, who felt he was being unfairly singled out. “You keep saying my name in every meeting,” complained Walker after a defeat at Liverpool. “Every fucking meeting it’s my name. You’ve somehow brought my name into it.”
Walker, who had been voted captain by his teammates, also claimed Guardiola did not want him to be skipper.
Guardiola responded by saying Walker was taking the issue too personally but also showed signs of emotion as he explained why he had extended his contract despite their poor run.
“If I am a problem you have to tell me,” said Guardiola in a broken voice. “I won’t stay here for the money or just for the fact of staying. I extended my contract because I want to be with you. I want to fight. I don’t want you to feel like I’m leaving or running away.”
![Pep Guardiola speaking to Kyle Walker in a break in play when Manchester City played Spurs in November 2024. The two clashed when Walker was captain.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/661e1db928a879acc88f18e1cf001a908a4d6c8c/414_137_2666_1819/master/2666.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Another extraordinary outburst came in November 2025 after a dismal 2-0 loss to Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League. Guardiola, whose decision to make 10 changes had backfired, threatened to quit in the dressing room afterwards.
He said: “It’s unacceptable this lack of courage, passion and love and desire to win and do it better. I work for you. I leave my life, my divorce and my family is away, and everything for all of you. And what do you give back? The fucking performance you have done. It’s a disgrace guys. I’m really fucking tired. When I see that I’m exhausted, I’m drained. I want to quit.”
after newsletter promotion
Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the Manchester City chair, recently said Guardiola must have threatened to leave “100 times” during his tenure but he too had his concerns after the Leverkusen game.
In a remarkable release of voice notes between Khaldoon and the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, the chair said he was “so angry” after “probably one of the lowest points we’ve had”. Soriano said the response should not be “too negative or aggressive” but “not too kind or accommodating either”.
The four-part series, which covers the past two seasons, also includes some frank boardroom discussions about transfer policy and the long-serving Kevin De Bruyne’s disappointment after being told his contract would not be renewed.
summary: A new Amazon Prime documentary, "A Beautiful Obsession," reveals behind-the-scenes turmoil at Manchester City during Pep Guardiola's difficult managerial run. The footage captures a dressing room argument between Guardiola and then-captain Kyle Walker, as well as moments where an emotional Guardiola threatened to quit. The four-part series also documents boardroom discussions, transfer policies, and Kevin De Bruyne's disappointment over his non-renewed contract.
key_points: Pep Guardiola clashed in the dressing room with captain Kyle Walker after a defeat at Liverpool.
Walker complained that Guardiola unfairly singled him out in every team meeting.
Guardiola threatened to quit and expressed exhaustion following a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Bayer Leverkusen in November 2025.
Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano exchanged voice notes expressing anger and concern after the Leverkusen match.
The documentary also covers Kevin De Bruyne's disappointment after learning his contract would not be renewed.
